correctness.rationale: Direct Gaussian characteristic functions yield exact cosine and sine variances and cross covariances for all real r in [-1,1]. The worst unknown-phase variance is half the larger of two closed-form diagonal covariance entries. On [-1,0] one decreases and the other increases, meeting uniquely at r=-log(2-exp(-q))/q; on (0,1] the sine entry strictly increases, so no second minimum exists. Exact endpoint and asymptotic comparisons follow algebraically. The supplied standard-library checker separately verifies 45 Gaussian double integrals and 6,611 finite-grid inequalities, supplementary to the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Unknown Fourier phase is a natural nuisance in variance reduction for random-walk heat solvers. The full minimax design yields a nontrivial unique interior correlation, strict superiority to both standard independent and fully antithetic Gaussian pairs at every q>0, a sharp crossover at q=log 3 between baseline endpoints, and an order-q to order-q^2 low-noise worst-phase variance improvement. This provides an exact spectral calibration benchmark, without claiming general nonlinear or multistep solver guarantees.
